recommendation.reason: Implement a hybrid liability model. Use an imported official Annual Business Registration and Tax Form total liability when present. Otherwise calculate Gross Receipts Tax from official 2025, 2026 and 2027 activity-category bands; calculate each activity category separately and sum. Keep HGR and OE as calculated components only when their specific inputs are present; the current combined HGR/OE applicability flag is sufficient for gating but not for computing those additional taxes. Keep sf_registration_fee_schedule_amount_cents as the preferred registration-fee input, with official fee-band fallback for supported registration years.

runtimeAlgorithm.plainEnglish: Use this as a liability/cost model, not a savings-benefit model. First, if sf_gross_receipts_tax_return_present is true and sf_business_tax_return_total_liability_cents is present from an official filed return or bill, return that amount as the authoritative annual business tax liability. Otherwise validate taxYear, map each activity to one of San Francisco Business Activity Categories 1 through 7, and require taxable San Francisco gross receipts by category after official exclusions and allocation/apportionment. Apply the small business exemption gate before computing GRT. If not exempt, calculate each category with the tax-year/category progressive rate table and sum category liabilities. For multiple activity categories, apply the official $10,000-or-less pre-allocation combining rule only if the pre-allocation category receipts are available; otherwise calculate each reported category separately and sum. HGR is an additional tax: calculate it only from HGR-specific taxable receipts by category or use an imported HGR component; do not calculate it from the current combined HGR/OE flag. OE is another additional tax: calculate it only if executive pay ratio, OE taxable receipts and exemption inputs are present, or use an imported OE component; otherwise gate. For registration fees, prefer sf_registration_fee_schedule_amount_cents from the official schedule/bill; if absent, use the official registration fee band for the supported registration year and basis receipts. For post-2026-27 registration years, import the CPI-adjusted official fee or keep gated.
pseudocode: if sf_allocated_gross_receipts_by_category missing or not marked taxable_after_exclusions_and_allocation: gate('missing taxable SF gross receipts by category')
threshold = sf_small_business_exemption_threshold_cents ?? (taxYear == 2025 ? 500000000 : gate('missing CPI-adjusted small business threshold'))
if smallBusinessExempt: grossReceiptsTax = 0 else grossReceiptsTax = sum(progressiveTax(receiptsByCategory[cat], grModel[taxYear][cat].bands) for cat in categories)

function progressiveTax(receiptsCents, bands): tax = 0; for band in bands: taxable = max(0, min(receiptsCents, band.ceilingCents ?? receiptsCents) - band.floorCents); tax += taxable * band.rateDecimal; return round(tax)

if sf_homelessness_gross_receipts_tax_cents != null: hgrTax = sf_homelessness_gross_receipts_tax_cents else if sf_hgr_taxable_gross_receipts_by_category present: hgrTax = sum(progressiveTax(hgrReceiptsByCategory[cat], hgrModel[taxYear][cat].bands) for cat in categories) else if sf_hgr_applies || sf_hgr_or_overpaid_executive_tax_applicability: gate('HGR applies or may apply but HGR-specific basis is missing') else hgrTax = 0

if sf_overpaid_executive_gross_receipts_tax_cents != null: oeTax = sf_overpaid_executive_gross_receipts_tax_cents else if OE inputs complete: if oeExempt or sf_overpaid_executive_pay_ratio <= 100: oeTax = 0 else oeTax = round(sf_overpaid_executive_taxable_gross_receipts_cents * selectedOeRate(taxYear, sf_overpaid_executive_pay_ratio)) else if sf_overpaid_executive_tax_applies || sf_hgr_or_overpaid_executive_tax_applicability: gate('OE applies or may apply but executive ratio/exemption inputs are missing') else oeTax = 0

repair.evidenceText: Repair target and current RetroFi inputs are from the uploaded prompt.  Official San Francisco guidance states that, for tax years beginning in 2025 after Prop M, Gross Receipts Tax is imposed on taxable San Francisco gross receipts, filed as part of the Annual Business Registration and Tax Form, and calculated by activity category and San Francisco receipts. ([Treasurer & Tax Collector][7]) Official Prop M and Annual Business Registration pages publish the 2025/2026 and 2027 gross receipts category rates. ([Treasurer & Tax Collector][2]) Official instructions and Code sources confirm the $5,000,000 2025 filing/small-business threshold, annual registration renewal requirement, multiple-category summing rule, and CPI adjustment for later small-business thresholds. ([Treasurer & Tax Collector][1]) Official HGR guidance publishes the HGR threshold, exclusions and category rates, and official OE guidance publishes the executive-pay-ratio rates and exemptions. ([Treasurer & Tax Collector][3]) Official Code Section 855, the 2025-2026 renewal instructions, and the annual form page publish registration fee schedules for the 2025-2026 transition and registration years beginning April 1, 2026, including the separate $4 state fee shown on the official form tables. ([American Legal Publishing][8])
unresolvedGaps: The currently collected sf_hgr_or_overpaid_executive_tax_applicability input does not distinguish HGR from OE and is not enough to compute either additional tax.

HGR should not be computed from ordinary GRT taxable receipts unless the system can confirm HGR-specific exclusions, including Commercial Rents Tax receipts and specified real-estate exclusions, have already been applied.
OE V1 computation requires executive pay ratio, OE taxable receipts and exemption inputs; otherwise import the filed OE component or gate the component.

The 2026 and later small-business exemption threshold is CPI-adjusted and rounded by statute; do not hard-code $5,000,000 for 2026 or 2027 if the official adjusted threshold has been published/imported.
Registration fees after the 2026-2027 registration year require the official CPI-adjusted schedule or an imported bill amount.

This model does not calculate Gross Receipts Tax credits, Commercial Rents Tax, Administrative Office Tax, penalties, interest or estimated-payment credits unless those amounts are imported from the filed return or supplied as separate official inputs.
